Triage is vacant in objectui and this is the lane's own programme follow-up (the gate the #7359 / PR #7427 claim promised as its own card), so the seat grades it, as it did #7359. Clause-②: no — a gate, no contract claim. Governed: any eval row that moves is `skills/objectui/**` ⇒ the PR stays DRAFT (ui#6866 批 #7); review requests are the seat's step.

Scope, exactly the card's three steps, with the two design inputs decided and argued rather than assumed:
1. The runner (its own script or a second phase of `scripts/check-skill-examples.mjs` — decide, and say why): every `must_contain` token of every `skills/objectui/evals/*.json` must occur as a WHOLE token (word-boundary or token-boundary match, never substring) in the oracle's guide set; `must_not_contain` is not validated against the guides (shape check at most). Exit 2 `PRECONDITION NOT MET` on an empty population, per #7427's convention; a `--self-test` with both directions (a taught token passes; an untaught one reds; a substring-only match reds; a `must_not_contain` entry does not red).
2. The oracle: measure BOTH (per-guide = `guides/BASENAME.md` matching the eval file; bundle-wide = the whole skill) in `--measure` mode, print the two red lists, and pick one with the four-axis reasoning below — the `registerComponent` row on `evals/page-builder.json` eval 1 is the known disagreement. ⛔ Do not rewrite guide prose to teach a token; ⛔ do not drop or re-point rows mechanically — list the red rows in the PR body as the honest starting list for a per-row follow-up, and land the gate opt-in / zero-red on day one (baseline the red rows the way `check-doc-fence-languages.mjs` baselines its declared files, shrink-only) unless the red list is empty under the chosen oracle.
3. Wire it like `skill-examples.yml` (own workflow, no `paths` / `paths-ignore`, `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` row in `scripts/dependabot-merge-gate.mjs`, `merge-queue-reporting.test.ts`, the `ci-cd-pipeline.md` inventory) or, if it is a phase of the existing gate, prove the existing workflow already runs it.
